text:
Anya: Quick sync  noticed a small but consistent 95p latency tail after we enabled continuous-batching v2 (CB2) in hosted canary last night. Not catastrophic but visible on dashboards.
Samir: I saw that. Short requests (<=8 tokens) have more queue wait. Metrics show increased batch_window_ms usage.
Maria: CB2 deliberately lengthens the aggregation window to improve throughput. That matches the signal. Curious why only some tenants are impacted.
Joel: We discovered a translation gap: Dedicated/Private adapters on older agent releases (v1.12-ish) don't understand the new 'cb2' feature flag. Control-plane currently drops unknown fields, so legacy runtimes get implicit legacy behavior while hosted runs CB2.
Anya: Right. That creates inconsistent behavior depending on which pool handles traffic. We need deterministic semantics across hosting modes.
Samir: Proposed mitigations: (A) Capability handshake: runtime declares supported_features, control-plane gate features by capability. (B) Translation mapping: when runtime lacks cb2, map it to explicit legacy knobs (batch_window_ms, max_batch_size). (C) Router labeling: route tenants to pools advertising desired features.
Maria: I worry about mapping semantics for KV cache warm-up. CB2's batching pattern influences KV caching and prefetch; naive mapping could impact quality. We'll need regression tests on prompt sets.
Joel: Implementing CB2 emulation in legacy runtime is risky. Prefer mapping at control-plane: translate cb2 -> concrete legacy parameters when runtime doesn't advertise cb2. That keeps semantics explicit.
infra-bot: Canary: CB2 rollout paused by infra-bot at 1787654300 for investigation. See https://deploys/redwood/CB2/pause.
Anya: Also, we should stop silently dropping unknown fields. Control-plane should emit a translation/audit event when a field is elided or mapped. That helps SRE and customers debug differences.
Samir: Agreed. Draft rule sample: 
````
# translation pseudo
if not adapter.supports('cb2'):
  map('batching_strategy=cb2') -> {"batch_window_ms":6, "max_batch_size":8}
else:
  propagate('cb2')
````
Maria: Add perf regression harness: run eval prompt set against v1.12 with mapped defaults and against CB2 hosted to compare latency and output quality (perplexity / eval metrics).
Joel: Router change: add pool_features metadata (e.g., {"cb2":"supported"}) and make the routing policy prefer feature-compatible pools when tenant opts-in. For Dedicated pools we can surface pool_features in the admin UI.
SRE-Oncall: From alerting POV, add a divergence monitor: if tenant-level 95p deviates >X ms from pool-level 95p, trigger pager after short window. That should catch translation-induced regressions quickly.
Anya: Who owns what: Samir -> capability handshake and audit events; Joel -> router pool_features and routing preference; Maria -> perf/regression harness and KV cache checks; I'll update runbook and coordinate canary control.
Samir: I'll send a PR with capability field + audit-event schema. Also suggest adding a short-lived 'cb2_strict_mode' feature-flag; when set, control-plane rejects translations and insists on exact runtime support (useful for debugging).
Maria: Regarding customer visibility: internal audit events first. Later we can offer enterprise telemetry export so customers can see when their config was mapped. Internal first minimizes noise.
Joel: Implementation note: translation idempotency test in manifests pipeline: control-plane config -> adapter manifest -> adapter decode -> canonical flags equals expected. Add unit test harness for that.
Anya: Also update manifests validator to warn if a requested feature is dropped. Make it fail in 'strict_mode'.
infra-bot: Canary pause recorded at 1787654300.
Samir: Estimated timelines: capability+audit PR by EOD +2, router changes ~1w, perf runs start today.
Maria: I'll run the KV cache warm-up simulations against v1.12 with mapped parameters and share diffs.
SRE-Oncall: Adding the divergence alert now, and a short escalation doc for PM/SE teams if customers report perf regressions.
Anya: Plan: 1) Pause canary (done), 2) Add capability negotiation + audit + mapping rules, 3) Run perf/regressions, 4) If stable resume canary with opt-in tenant flag (enable_cb2: true), 5) Monitor divergence alerts closely.
Samir: Posting PR link in #eng-runtime in ~3 hours.
Joel: I'll prototype pool_features label and add router preference logic; will need a short migration for pool metadata.
Maria: We'll measure both latency and output fidelity (eval suite) before approving resume.
Anya: Thanks. Let's avoid surprising enterprise tenants; default behavior should favor parity over throughput until we fully validate. Ping me when PRs land and we'll coordinate canary resume. :thumbsup:
